\chapter{It's Getting Late}
\label{ch:hi-getting-late}
\hlchaptermodality{122}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say it has got late and I have to go, ask leave politely, and talk about a holiday.}

Complete HI-C122-jana-hai: excuse yourself politely.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[chuṭṭī]{\hi{छुट्टी} (chuṭṭī) — a holiday, a day off, leave}

\label{lesson:HI-C122-chhutti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for come again, then the Hindi for let's go.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{छुट्टी}}
\textbf{\hi{छुट्टी}} (\emph{chuṭṭī}) — \textquotedblleft{}a holiday\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}a day off\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}leave from work\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{आज} \hi{छुट्टी} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}today is a holiday\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\hi{आज}} you know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A day off.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chuṭṭī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chuṭṭī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{āj chuṭṭī hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for come again, then the Hindi for let's go, then say \emph{chuṭṭī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{छुट्टी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A holiday, a day off, leave\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[der ho gaī]{\hi{देर} \hi{हो} \hi{गई} (der ho gaī) — it has got late}

\label{lesson:HI-C122-derhogai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for let's go, then the Hindi for a holiday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{देर} \hi{हो} \hi{गई}}
\textbf{\hi{देर} \hi{हो} \hi{गई}} (\emph{der ho gaī}) — \textquotedblleft{}it has got late\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}I am late\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{देर}} is the lateness you know; \textbf{\hi{हो} \hi{गई}} is \textquotedblleft{}has become\textquotedblright{}. The first reason to leave.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A reason to go.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{der ho gaī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{der ho gaī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{der ho gaī}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for let's go, then the Hindi for a holiday, then say \emph{der ho gaī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{देर} \hi{हो} \hi{गई} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}It has got late\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\label{lesson:HI-C122-aramse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a holiday, then the Hindi for it has got late.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{आराम} \hi{से}}
\textbf{\hi{आराम} \hi{से}} (\emph{ārām se}) — \textquotedblleft{}comfortably\textquotedblright{}, and as a parting, \textquotedblleft{}take it easy\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{आराम}} is the rest you know, with \textbf{\hi{से}}, \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\hi{आराम} \hi{से} \hi{बैठिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}sit comfortably\textquotedblright{}; at the door, \textbf{\hi{आराम} \hi{से}} alone is \textquotedblleft{}take it easy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An unhurried goodbye.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[ijāzat]{\hi{इजाज़त} (ijāzat) — permission, leave to go}

\label{lesson:HI-C122-ijazat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for it has got late, then the Hindi for take it easy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{इजाज़त}}
\textbf{\hi{इजाज़त}} (\emph{ijāzat}) — \textquotedblleft{}permission\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{अब} \hi{इजाज़त} \hi{दीजिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}now please give me leave to go\textquotedblright{}, the most courteous way to excuse yourself from a host.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A formal way out of a room.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for it has got late, then the Hindi for take it easy, then say \emph{ijāzat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[jānā hai]{\hi{जाना} \hi{है} (jānā hai) — (I) have to go}

\label{lesson:HI-C122-janahai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for take it easy, then the Hindi for permission to go.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{जाना} \hi{है}}
\textbf{\hi{जाना} \hi{है}} (\emph{jānā hai}) — \textquotedblleft{}have to go\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{जाना} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I have to go\textquotedblright{}, with the person in \textbf{\hi{मुझे}}. \textbf{\hi{जाना}} is \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A holiday, it's late, take it easy, leave to go, I have to go.
\end{grammarlens}
